terra.problem: The reference given does not support the statement that David later became Israel's king; that fact needs its own reference.
The text does not say that nobody picked up a shovel or that rolling stones was faster than digging.
The line about Joshua not wanting anyone to admire the stones attributes a thought to him that the text does not give.
The passage says the army returned to camp, but it does not say the men rested later.
The joke about knowing ships from bubbles in dough has no clear connection and does not pass the joke logic test.
The text says no one dared speak against the Israelites, not that the whole land went quiet or that no grumble of any kind was heard.
Joshua summons the men of Israel, but the text does not say everybody watched or that the whole army saw the commanders' action.
The Gibeonites are not named in this scene, but the text does not establish that none were present.
Joshua orders the bodies taken down and thrown into the cave; the text does not say he ordered the later placement of the stones.
The statement about what the writer wants the reader to see adds an unstated intention and implies the action was not also Joshua's own idea.
The fortified cities where survivors retreated do not establish that the kings' cities had walls, so the text does not necessarily point the other way.
The guess about a night's sleep adds a time and an event the passage does not give.
